author: Maggy McGuigan
title: New stormwater requirements delay Glenwood Town Center development - NewsBreak
text:
By Maggy McGuigan ,
1 days ago
PANAMA CITY, Fla. (WMBB) – New statewide stormwater management rules are delaying progress on the Glenwood Town Center.
Back in July, Panama City officials granted the Sankofa Group the development agreement for the town center.
Panama City approves $30M Glenwood Town Center development The plans include apartments, a grocery store, and eventually townhomes.
The Sankofa Group was given six months to develop a buildable site plan, but FDOT recently updated its stormwater requirements. So, Sankofa officials asked for a five-month extension to the due diligence period to address engineering concerns.
“They need to narrow down and determine a path forward for stormwater mitigation. The site is located at the intersection of MLK Boulevard and Highway 98, 15th Street. Both are Florida Department of Transportation roads, and they get to determine what the shots are. The stormwater mitigation requirements have been increased,” Panama City CRA Board Member Janice Lucas said.
A study in November identified a stormwater retention issue associated with the proposed development.
Several potential stormwater solutions were identified with preliminary cost estimates ranging from $890,000 to $1.8 million, depending on the approach selected.
Board members approved the extension Tuesday night, which will give Sankofa officials time to refine the project and determine how much the stormwater mitigation will cost.
“He has been working diligently, looking to acquire more land in the surrounding area for the site, as well as working with engineers, both with the city and Anchor Engineering, whom he hired to be the project lead for engineering on the Glenwood Town Center side,” Lucas said.
Any stormwater costs will be paid by the developer.
CRA board members say there are no changes to the design of the town center as of right now.
The plans include both apartments and townhomes, 20% of which will be set aside for people making no more than 80% of Bay County’s median income.
CRA board members hope that after this five-month extension, they can move forward with land clearing and construction.
There is a three-phase design plan that’s estimated to be completed in six to seven years.
